subsystems.name: Robot unit
subsystems.role: the minimal agent — cheap, robust and expendable in large numbers.
parts: motor drivers and wheels or rotors

subsystems.name: Local communication mesh
subsystems.role: lets robots exchange messages only with nearby neighbours, so no central node is required.

subsystems.name: Stigmergic field
subsystems.role: a shared virtual environment where robots leave and read digital pheromone markers.

subsystems.name: Decentralised control
subsystems.role: turns simple local rules into coordinated group behaviour.

subsystems.name: Power and docking
subsystems.role: keeps hundreds of small robots charged without human intervention.

subsystems.name: Mission interface
subsystems.role: lets a human set goals and monitor the swarm at a high level.

buildSteps.title: Define the swarm task
buildSteps.detail: Decide what the group must achieve — mapping an area, moving goods, or searching rubble — and the behaviours needed to achieve it.

buildSteps.title: Design the minimal robot
buildSteps.detail: Choose sensors, actuators and compute small enough and cheap enough that losing some units is acceptable.

buildSteps.title: Implement local communication
buildSteps.detail: Build a radio or infrared link that lets each robot talk only to neighbours within range.

buildSteps.title: Create the virtual pheromone model
buildSteps.detail: Define how digital markers are deposited, read, and allowed to decay or diffuse over time.

buildSteps.title: Write local interaction rules
buildSteps.detail: Program each robot to react to its neighbours and to pheromone levels, producing swarm behaviour without a central controller.

buildSteps.title: Simulate at scale
buildSteps.detail: Test hundreds or thousands of virtual robots to find parameter settings that stay stable and efficient.

buildSteps.title: Build and calibrate the physical swarm
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the robots, calibrate sensors, and tune communication ranges so real units match simulation.

buildSteps.title: Validate in a controlled environment
buildSteps.detail: Run the swarm on a bounded task such as warehouse shelving or a mock disaster site, measuring completion and failure rates.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with human oversight
buildSteps.detail: Place the swarm in real operations with a supervisor able to pause, redirect or shut it down.

prerequisites.why: hundreds of units are only practical if each robot is cheap to build and replace.
robots need to pass messages without a central access point.
many behaviours work in simulation, but real-world noise and latency still cause failures.
each robot must know roughly where it is and avoid neighbours in crowded, changing spaces.
docking and battery management must work without human help for long missions.

pathway.milestone: laboratory swarms of tens to hundreds of small robots and large-scale simulations
pathway.unlocks: proof that decentralised rules can produce useful group behaviour.

pathway.milestone: warehouse fleets that self-allocate tasks and routes instead of following a central scheduler
pathway.unlocks: more resilient logistics that keep working when individual robots fail.

pathway.milestone: disaster-response swarms that map buildings and locate survivors
pathway.unlocks: faster situational awareness where infrastructure is damaged.
adaptive structures and environmental monitoring at scales no single robot could cover.
